classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the concentrate volume stays constant while the total changes, then use the unitary method to find the new total and extra water.

content.prompt: A girl makes up a cordial drink so that $10\%$ of the drink is cordial concentrate. The rest is water. The girl has $350\text{ mL}$ of the drink in a jug. She now decides that she wants the cordial concentrate content to be only $8\%$. How much extra water does she need to put in the jug?

answer.short:
$87.5\text{ mL}$

The concentrate stays at $35\text{ mL}$; use this as $8\%$ of the new drink volume.
answer.worked:
Adding water leaves the volume of cordial concentrate unchanged.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Concentrate volume}&=\frac{10}{100}\times350\text{ mL}\\\text{Concentrate volume}&=35\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$

This is $8\%$ of the new drink volume.

$$\begin{align*}1\%\text{ of the new volume}&=\frac{35}{8}\text{ mL}\\100\%\text{ of the new volume}&=\frac{35}{8}\times100\text{ mL}\\100\%\text{ of the new volume}&=437.5\text{ mL}\\\text{Extra water}&=(437.5-350)\text{ mL}\\\text{Extra water}&=87.5\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
